item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 14, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Schools Board of Education is scheduled to meet on September 15, 2026, to approve its agenda and recognize individuals.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet on September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education is scheduled to hold a meeting on September 15, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building. The agenda includes a welcome, call to order, pledge, roll call, and approval or modification of the agenda.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to finance a portion of the 48" Supply Water Transmission Project. This resolution would allow the city to finance a portion of the 48" Supply Water Transmission Project with bonds purchased by the Arkansas Development Finance Authority in the amount of $9,621,360.00, with $887,911.00 of that principal amount in the form of a principal forgiveness bond.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 201 SW E Street from single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed rezoning would change the property at 201 SW E Street from allowing only suburban single-family homes to a 'Neighborhood Edge' designation, which typically permits a wider variety of housing types and mixed uses.
On the Bella Vista Board of Zoning Adjustment agenda: Board to consider a variance for a non-residential structure at 19 Cheviot Place. This would allow a detached nonresidential structure at 19 Cheviot Place to be placed differently than current rules allow. This could affect the appearance or use of the property.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11 in Bentonville. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled to take place on October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of the larger Big Sugar Classic week.
Bat discovery delays Pea Ridge sidewalk construction. Construction of a sidewalk on McCulloch Street in Pea Ridge is facing delays due to the discovery of bats living in nearby trees.
Pea Ridge leaders plan to preserve Rich family homestead. Pea Ridge leaders are developing plans for a natural park on the property of the former Rich family homestead. Mayor Nathan See aims to preserve the natural setting of the historic site.
Fayetteville City Council to consider vendor for Lake Fayetteville marina shop. The Fayetteville City Council is scheduled to vote on the approval of a new vendor for the Lake Fayetteville marina rental and concession shop. The space has been vacant for approximately nine months.
Fayetteville City Council to consider aquatic center site study funding. The Fayetteville City Council is expected to consider allocating up to $75,000 for an additional assessment of potential site locations for the aquatic center. The aquatic center was approved as part of this year's bond package.
Springdale Fire chief discusses new station for city growth. The Springdale Fire Chief stated that a new fire station is intended to help the department keep pace with the city's growth in residents and expanding city limits.
Simmons Foods CEO discusses generational perspective. Todd Simmons, CEO of Simmons Foods, expressed his focus on a 'generational perspective' in his role. He has been CEO for over a decade.
Washington Regional hires new physicians. Fayetteville-based Washington Regional has announced new physician hires. Rogers-based Generations Bank also announced new hires and promotions.
Springdale hosts annual Squirrel Cook-off. The annual World Champion Squirrel Cook-off returned to Springdale on Saturday. The event featured various squirrel-based dishes.
Nonprofit builds beds for Northwest Arkansas children. A local nonprofit chapter constructed 250 beds for children in Northwest Arkansas. The organization aims to ensure that no children in the area sleep on the floor.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 13, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Schools Board of Education will meet on September 15, 2026, to approve its agenda and recognize individuals.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education will hold a meeting on September 15, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building. The agenda includes a welcome, roll call, approval of the agenda, and recognitions.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11 in Bentonville. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of the larger Big Sugar Classic week.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to finance a portion of the 48" Supply Water Transmission Project. This resolution would allow the city to finance a portion of a large water transmission project with bonds purchased by the Arkansas Development Finance Authority, including a principal forgiveness bond of $887,911.00.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 201 SW E Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood edge.. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development at 201 SW E Street, moving from single-family homes to a neighborhood edge style within a walkable neighborhood.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider requiring 200-foot distance between short-term rentals in residential zones. This proposal would mean that new short-term rentals in residential areas would need to be at least 200 feet away from any existing short-term rental. This could affect where new short-term rental properties can be established in the city.
Centerton's downtown master plan requires public-private partnerships. Centerton officials state that the city's Downtown Master Plan will necessitate public-private partnerships for its revitalization and expansion. The city is currently determining the next steps after about a year of planning.
Colliers Arkansas announces additions and promotion to Northwest Arkansas team. Colliers Arkansas has announced four new additions and one promotion to its Northwest Arkansas team. The team is based in Rogers at 3503 S. 55th St., Suite 200.
GoodWorks hosts inaugural Day of service with 14 nonprofits. GoodWorks, a volunteer center of the Jones Center, hosted its first Day of Service on Saturday. The event connected residents with 14 local nonprofits to support volunteerism across Northwest Arkansas.
Volunteers build 250 beds for Northwest Arkansas children. Volunteers in Bentonville built 250 beds for children in Northwest Arkansas as part of the annual Bunks Across America event by Sleep in Heavenly Peace. This initiative aims to provide beds for children who need them.
XNA transitions from zero security to modern TSA standards. Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) has evolved from having no security to implementing modern Transportation Security Administration (TSA) standards. This change reflects the normalization of security procedures for travelers.
Concerns raised about ICE operations' impact on Northwest Arkansas businesses. Irma Chavez, founder of the Arkansas Hispanic Chamber of Commerce, has expressed concerns about the impact of nationwide enhanced immigration enforcement on Northwest Arkansas businesses. She noted that small and family-owned businesses are particularly vulnerable.
Northwest Arkansas Food Bank and cystic fibrosis foundation hold fundraising events. The Northwest Arkansas Food Bank held its second annual Flavor of Giving fundraiser on August 27 at Osage House in Cave Springs. The Cystic Fibrosis Foundation also hosted an event to raise funds for local causes.
Erik Dees releases new book on values-driven leadership. Erik Dees, a partner at Fayetteville-based Milestone Leadership, has released a new book titled "Keeper of the Culture." The book challenges leaders to redefine success and what constitutes strong leadership.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 12, 2026
item.description:
Benton County has reached exceptional drought status for the first time since 2012.
Benton County reaches exceptional drought status. Parts of Benton County have been upgraded to exceptional drought status, marking the third time the area has experienced such severe dryness since 2012.
Benton washington regional public water authority lifts irrigation moratorium. The Benton Washington Regional Public Water Authority has lifted a weeks-long moratorium on lawn watering for its customers.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet on September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education will hold a meeting on September 15, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building, 500 Tiger Blvd.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 201 SW E Street from single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development than suburban single-family homes at 201 SW E Street, potentially increasing housing density in the area.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider new distance requirements for short-term rentals. This proposal would require short-term rentals in residential zones to be at least 200 feet apart from each other. This could affect the availability and location of short-term rental properties in your neighborhood.
Centerton to host 49th annual Centerton Days event. The 49th annual Centerton Days celebration will take place this weekend, offering a range of activities.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11 in Bentonville. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Water for Good to host Grounds for Good coffee crawl in Bentonville. Faith-based nonprofit Water for Good will host its inaugural Grounds for Good coffee crawl in October in Bentonville.
Bentonville Public Library continues stories we share series. The Bentonville Public Library honored Rock Van Winkle with a film screening and panel discussion as part of its Stories We Share series.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 11, 2026
item.description:
A new traffic signal is now operating at the intersection of East Central Avenue and McCollum Road in Bentonville.
Bentonville activates new traffic signal. A new traffic signal has begun operation at the intersection of East Central Avenue and McCollum Road in Bentonville.
Bentonville to host Made in America Contested Logistics Summit. Leaders from multiple industries are gathering in Bentonville for the Made in America Contested Logistics Summit.
Bella Vista celebrates 10 years of bike trails. Bella Vista is commemorating the 10th anniversary of its bike trail system with festivities planned over the coming months.
Cobb research initiative names 2026 grant recipients. Siloam Springs-based Cobb-Vantress LLC has selected eight projects to receive funding through its research initiative.
Harps food stores announces leadership changes. Harps Food Stores, a Northwest Arkansas-based grocery chain, has announced two new leadership appointments.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee - Changed Due to Labor Day Holiday agenda: Girls on the Run Fall Celebratory 5K to be held on November 14, 2026. This informational item concerns a 5K race that will use the same route as last year, taking place from 7 AM to 12 PM, with the race beginning at 8:15 AM.
Bentonville Schools Board of education schedules meeting. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education Meeting is scheduled for September 15, 2026.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Tyson foods' schomburger buys company shares. New Tyson CEO Donnie D. Schomburger has purchased 19,450 shares of company stock.
Bentonville beats Fayetteville in tennis match. The Bentonville tennis team defeated Fayetteville despite a brief disruption from rain.
Bentonville West downs Fort Smith Northside in volleyball. The Bentonville West volleyball team defeated Fort Smith Northside after taking control in the third set.
Buffalo River Aviation receives air carrier certificate. Bentonville-based Buffalo River Aviation Services LLC has received its Federal Aviation Administration Part 135 air carrier certificate.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 10, 2026
item.description:
A new traffic signal on East Central Avenue in Bentonville will become fully operational next week.
Bentonville to activate new Central Avenue traffic signal. A new traffic signal at East Central Avenue and McCollum Road in Bentonville will be placed in flash mode before becoming fully operational next week.
Bentonville Schools Board of education schedules meeting. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education has scheduled a meeting for September 15, 2026. No agenda has been posted for this meeting yet.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 201 SW E Street from single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development than suburban single-family homes at 201 SW E Street, potentially introducing more varied housing options or small-scale commercial uses in the area.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee - Changed Due to Labor Day Holiday agenda: Girls on the Run Fall Celebratory 5K to use same route as last year. Residents should be aware of the Girls on the Run NWA Fall Celebratory 5K, which will take place on November 14, 2026, from 7 AM to 12 PM, with the race beginning at 8:15 AM, and will use the same route as the previous year.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider amending various sections of the community Code. These amendments could change the rules and regulations that govern development, land use, and other aspects of the city's planning, affecting residents and businesses throughout Bentonville.
Benton County judge discusses transition process. Benton County Judge Barry Moehring stated that he will remain in office temporarily and assist with the transition process if Austin McCollum does not take the oath of office.
Crystal Bridges to host Condoleezza Rice and Norah O’Donnell. Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art in Bentonville announced that former Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice and '60 Minutes' correspondent Norah O’Donnell will speak as part of its fall Building Bridges speaker series.
Crystal Bridges announces Building Bridges speaker lineup. Crystal Bridges announced the fall lineup for its Building Bridges series, which will feature conversations celebrating the American spirit and diverse perspectives, including former Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice and an Emmy Award-winning journalist.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville, as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
XNA nominated for USA Today's best small airport. Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) has been nominated for USA Today's best small airport.
Springdale City Council approves $5 million for East Emma Avenue project. The Springdale City Council has authorized $5 million in construction contracts for a project to reduce the number of lanes on East Emma Avenue.
Frisco Inferno BBQ Competition returns to Rogers. The 11th Annual Frisco Inferno Barbecue Competition will return to Rogers as part of Bikes, Blues and BBQ.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 9, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville City Council denied a rezoning request for a Northwest Fifth Street property after public comments.
Heat Advisory issued for Benton County until 7 PM CDT. A Heat Advisory is in effect for Benton County until 7 PM CDT, with heat index values expected to reach up to 109 degrees.
Bentonville City Council denies rezoning request. The Bentonville City Council voted to deny a rezoning request for a Northwest Fifth Street property, which sought to change from single-family residential to mixed-use zoning.
Bentonville announces Southeast A Street closure for sewer work. Southeast A Street in Bentonville will close starting Thursday for sewer work.
Bentonville street to close for over a year as part of long-term project. A street in southern Bentonville will be closed for more than a year, beginning today, as part of a long-term project.
Bentonville High School opens Crossland Construction Lab. Bentonville High School has opened a new Crossland Construction Lab, part of an effort to introduce students to industry jobs.
Rogers mixed-income community opens after $13 million investment. The three-story, 60-unit Olive Street Apartments, a mixed-income community in Rogers, has opened following a $13 million investment.
Benton Washington regional public Water authority extends irrigation moratorium. The Benton Washington Regional Public Water Authority has extended water use restrictions for irrigation through at least the end of the week.
Bentonville seeks residents for Airport Advisory Board. The City of Bentonville is looking for qualified residents to serve on its Airport Advisory Board.
Bentonville Schools Board of Education meeting scheduled for September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education Meeting is scheduled for September 15, 2026.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11 in Bentonville. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee - Changed Due to Labor Day Holiday agenda: Girls on the Run Fall Celebratory 5K to use city streets on November 14, 2026. The committee will receive information about the Girls on the Run NWA Fall Celebratory 5K, which plans to use the same route as last year from 7 AM to 12 PM, with the race starting at 8:15 AM.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 8, 2026
item.description:
A Heat Advisory is in effect for Benton County until 8 PM CDT tonight, with heat index values expected to reach up to 109 degrees.
Heat Advisory issued for Benton county. A Heat Advisory has been issued for Benton County until 8 PM CDT tonight, with heat index values anticipated to reach up to 109 degrees. The advisory covers portions of northwest and west central Arkansas and east central, northeast, and southeast Oklahoma.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee - Changed Due to Labor Day Holiday agenda: Girls on the Run Fall Celebratory 5K to be held on November 14, 2026. This informational item concerns a 5K race that would use the same route as last year, taking place from 7 AM to 12 PM with the race beginning at 8:15 AM.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education Meeting is scheduled for September 15, 2026.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Mercy and Arkansas department of human services to launch maternal life360 program. Mercy and the Arkansas Department of Human Services will launch the Maternal Life360 program to promote healthier pregnancies. The collaboration aims to improve maternal and infant outcomes in Arkansas.
Bentonville High School seniors create STEM nonprofit. Bentonville High School seniors have established a new nonprofit to connect children with learning opportunities in science, technology, engineering, and math.
Police educate public on e-bike safety. Pea Ridge police are working to educate youth and parents about the safe use of electric bicycles as their popularity increases, particularly among students.
Bentonville tops conway in football. The Bentonville Tigers maintained their top spot in the Arkansas Sports Media Poll after defeating Conway in a battle of the state's top two teams.
Har-Ber quarterback Owens scores six touchdowns. Brice Owens was responsible for scoring six touchdowns for Springdale Har-Ber in a 45-14 win against Fort Smith Northside.
Outdoor events scheduled for Saturday. Saturday is packed with outdoor events, including a Springdale summer campout.
Stripers and walleye biting in NWA. Despite the heat, striped bass fishing remains steady in Beaver Lake, according to fishing guide Jon Conklin.
The War and Treaty to perform at walton arts center. Soul duo The War and Treaty are scheduled to return to Fayetteville for a performance at the Walton Arts Center.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 7, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory is in effect for Benton County until 7:00 PM CDT today, with heat index values expected to reach up to 109 degrees.
Heat advisory issued for Benton County. The National Weather Service has issued a heat advisory for Benton County until 7:00 PM CDT on September 7, with heat index values expected to reach up to 109 degrees.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 405 NW 5th Street from single-family to neighborhood node. This proposed change would allow for more diverse development, such as small-scale commercial or mixed-use buildings, in an area currently zoned for suburban single-family homes. The Planning Commission recommended approval with a 4-2 vote.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee - Changed Due to Labor Day Holiday agenda: Girls on the Run Fall Celebratory 5K to be held on November 14, 2026. This informational item provides details about the Girls on the Run NWA Fall Celebratory 5K, which would use the same route as last year, running from 7 AM to 12 PM with the race beginning at 8:15 AM.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to accept a $2,000,000 grant for Vaughn Road improvements. Accepting this grant would provide $2,000,000 in federal funding for the construction of improvements at the Hwy 12/279 Intersection. A budget adjustment would be needed to incorporate these funds.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet on September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education Meeting is scheduled for September 15, 2026.
Centerton to hold 49th annual Centerton Days celebration. Centerton will host its 49th annual Centerton Days celebration and parade on September 11 and 12, featuring two days of events, food, music, and activities.
Drift NWA returns to Drake Field on September 13. Drift NWA will bring drivers, competition, ride-alongs, food trucks, and vendors to Drake Field on September 13 for a family-friendly drifting event.
Northwest Arkansas school districts work to engage Gen Z students. Northwest Arkansas school districts are implementing strategies to keep Gen Z students engaged and prepared for future careers, according to a Walton Family Foundation study.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 6, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory is in effect for Benton County until 7:00 PM CDT today, with heat index values expected to reach up to 109 degrees.
Heat advisory issued for Benton county. The National Weather Service has issued a Heat Advisory for Benton County until 7:00 PM CDT today, September 6. Heat index values are expected to reach up to 109 degrees.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee - Changed Due to Labor Day Holiday agenda: Girls on the Run Fall Celebratory 5K on November 14th. The race will use the same route as last year and run from 7am to 12pm on November 14th, 2026, with the race beginning at 8:15am. Roads along the route will be affected during that time.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education has scheduled a meeting for September 15, 2026. An agenda for the meeting has not yet been posted.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. The event is part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Haag Brown commercial adds marketing leader to Northwest Arkansas office. Alley Harjo has joined real estate developer Haag Brown Commercial's Northwest Arkansas office. Harjo will serve as a marketing and creative leader for the company.
Drought conditions may impact autumn foliage in Northwest Arkansas. Autumn foliage in Northwest Arkansas may be less colorful this year if drought conditions persist. The lack of vibrant leaves could also affect tourism.
Washington Regional recognized on becker's list. Washington Regional has been named to a list compiled by Becker's.
America's Car-Mart approaches creditor deadline. Rogers-based America's Car-Mart faces a deadline set by its creditors to meet financial metrics. Failure to meet these metrics could result in a default on its loans.
NWACC's brightwater to offer free food training. Northwest Arkansas Community College's Brightwater culinary school will offer free food training. This opportunity is made possible through a grant from the Walton Family Foundation.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 5, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory is in effect for Benton County until 7:00 PM CDT on September 5.
Heat advisory issued for Benton County. The National Weather Service in Tulsa, Oklahoma, issued a heat advisory for Benton County until 7:00 PM CDT on September 5. The advisory is in effect for multiple counties in Arkansas and Oklahoma.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone property at 405 NW 5th Street. This would change the zoning of the property from suburban single-family to a neighborhood node classification, which could allow for different types of development than single-family homes.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee - Changed Due to Labor Day Holiday agenda: Girls on the Run Fall Celebratory 5K to be held on November 14, 2026. This item provides information about the Girls on the Run NWA Fall Celebratory 5K, which would use the same route as last year and take place from 7 AM to 12 PM, with the race beginning at 8:15 AM.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to approve a change order for the 12-inch water main reroute project. This would approve an additional $22,955.00 for the water main reroute project, covering costs for relocated water meters, fence removal, temporary gate installation, a final cut and cap, and a culvert addition. The original contract price was $694,210.99.
Arkansas Department of Transportation opens $400 million in highways. The Arkansas Department of Transportation opened $400 million in interstate-style highway projects in Northwest Arkansas. This includes a new stretch of Interstate 42 and a direct connector to Northwest Arkansas National Airport.
Walmart to deliver dunkin’ drinks and food. Walmart will begin delivering Dunkin’ drinks and food.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. The event is part of Big Sugar Classic week.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 4, 2026
item.description:
The Cave Springs Planning Commission approved a site development plan for the city's first Walmart Neighborhood Market and gas station.
Cave Springs Planning Commission approves Walmart Neighborhood Market plan. The Cave Springs Planning Commission approved a site development plan for a Walmart Neighborhood Market and gas station, moving the city closer to having its first such store.
Benton County Planning board of appeals overturns cell tower denial. The Benton County Planning Board of Appeals overturned a previous decision, allowing a proposed 150-foot-tall telecommunications tower to be built.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to consider rezoning 405 NW 5th Street. This proposed ordinance would change the zoning of the property at 405 NW 5th Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family, to T4.2, Neighborhood Node, which could allow for different types of development than currently permitted.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to accept a $2,000,000 grant for Vaughn Road improvements. This resolution would authorize the acceptance of a $2,000,000 grant to help fund the construction of the Hwy 12/279 Intersection Improvements project.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to approve a change order for the 12-inch water main reroute project. This resolution would approve Change Order #1 for the 12-inch Water Main Reroute project, adding $22,955.00 to the original contract price of $694,210.99 for work including water meter relocation, fence removal, and a culvert addition.
Tyson Foods lowers 2026 revenue guidance. Tyson Foods Inc. lowered its revenue growth guidance for 2026 due to significant margin pressure from the cattle industry.
7 Brew acquires 73 Salad and Go locations for $143.2 million. Springdale-based 7 Brew won a bankruptcy auction to acquire 73 locations of the Salad and Go chain for $143.2 million.
Crystal bridges museum announces new jewelry and gemstone exhibition. Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art announced an upcoming exhibition that will feature historically significant jewelry and gemstones.
Walmart senior advisor Jane Ewing to join Nike. Jane Ewing, a senior advisor and executive board member for ethics and compliance in Walmart's China operations, is leaving the company to join Nike.
Northwest and central Arkansas metros lead state job growth. Northwest Arkansas and central Arkansas continue to be the primary areas for job growth in the state, with year-over-year job gains of 2.6% and 1.3% respectively in July.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 3, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Planning Commission approved plans for the Bentonville Health Care Campus.
Bentonville Planning Commission approves health care campus plans. The Bentonville Health Care Campus moved closer to reality after the city planning commission approved its plans.
Benton County Planning Board rejects communication tower project. The Benton County Planning Board rejected an application for a 195-foot-tall telecommunications tower at 9689 E. Arkansas 72 in Bentonville.
Rogers Planning Commission approves rezoning for Anime Cafe beverage truck. The Rogers Planning Commission approved a rezoning request, allowing the Anime Cafe to operate its beverage truck in a new location.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville, as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Fayetteville's herman's ribhouse to reopen Thursday. Herman's Ribhouse, a historic Fayetteville restaurant, is scheduled to reopen on Thursday, September 3.
Fayetteville startup pub crawl to return in late September. A Fayetteville pub crawl that connects area companies with the community is scheduled to return in late September.
Engage NWA hosts Teen Volunteer Fair at Bentonville Public Library. Engage NWA held its annual Teen Volunteer Fair at the Bentonville Public Library as part of Welcoming Week NWA, an event organized with the Northwest Arkansas Council.
Northwest Arkansas Imagination Library needs local funding. Dolly Parton's Imagination Library in Northwest Arkansas lacks sufficient local funding to meet demand, despite increasing enrollment.
Siloam Springs Board of Directors discusses Flock camera usage. The Siloam Springs Board of Directors received a presentation from the Siloam Springs Police Department regarding the use of Flock safety cameras.
Fayetteville reminds businesses to renew licenses. The city of Fayetteville is reminding businesses to renew their business licenses.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission Work Session agenda: Commission to consider requiring 200-foot separation between short-term rentals. This proposed change would mean that short-term rentals, like Airbnbs, could not be located within 200 feet of each other in any residential area of the city. This could affect the availability and distribution of short-term rental properties in your neighborhood.
On the Bentonville Airport Advisory Board agenda: Airport advisory board to receive updates on various airport activities and city initiatives. Residents would learn about Airport Webpage Upgrades, upcoming events like the Game Aerospace & Bell Helicopter Event and the Arkansas Airport Operators Association Conference, Fuel Tank Cleaning, feedback on the Snow and Ice Management Plan, the Eastside Hangar Development, and cranes along I-49 S related to the Alice Walton Hospital Campus (Ref # 2026-ASW-10595-OE), as well as a 2026 Budget Update.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 2, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Planning Commission approved plans for the Bentonville Health Care Campus in a 6-0 vote.
Bentonville Planning Commission approves healthcare campus plans. The Bentonville Planning Commission approved plans for the Bentonville Health Care Campus in a 6-0 vote. There was no public dissent regarding the proposal.
Northwest Arkansas Community College enrollment exceeds 12,000 students. Northwest Arkansas Community College reported fall enrollment has surpassed 12,000 students for the first time.
Benton County average weekly wages increase by 8.9%. Average weekly wages in Benton County increased by 8.9% in the first quarter of 2026. This accounts for over 50% of the net increase in Arkansas' total wages paid during the same period.
On the Bentonville Library Advisory Board agenda: Public comments on agenda items. Residents can speak for up to 3 minutes on items on the agenda, provided they register with their name, address, phone number, and email address.
On the Bentonville Airport Advisory Board agenda: Airport advisory board to receive updates from the city of Bentonville Airport Manager. Residents would hear about various airport activities and plans, including Airport Webpage Upgrades, upcoming events like the Game Aerospace & Bell Helicopter Event and the Arkansas Airport Operators Association Conference, Fuel Tank Cleaning, the Snow and Ice Management Plan, Eastside Hangar Development, and a 2026 Budget Update, as well as information on cranes along I-49 S related to the Alice Walton Hospital Campus.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of Big Sugar Classic week.
HFG Architecture relocates Bentonville office to Rogers. HFG Architecture, a healthcare architecture and design firm, has relocated its Bentonville office to a 1,000-square-foot space in Rogers. Josh Danish has been named managing director of the new office.
Fayetteville City Council re-approves rezoning despite opposition. The Fayetteville City Council approved a rezoning for a property northwest of North Deane Solomon Road and West Vanike Drive for a second time. The approval occurred despite continued opposition from neighbors.
Springdale announces two road closures through mid-November. The city of Springdale announced two road closures that are expected to last through mid-November. Motorists are advised to be aware of these closures.
Fayetteville to operate cooling center all week. The city of Fayetteville announced it will operate a community cooling center during hot afternoons expected throughout the week. Heat indices above 100 degrees are anticipated.
Kestrel launches real estate portfolio management platform. Cash East launched Kestrel, a Fayetteville-based real estate portfolio management platform. The platform is designed to provide investors with financial oversight.
Northwest Arkansas Fall Job Fair to be held in Rogers. The Northwest Arkansas Fall Job Fair will take place in Rogers on Wednesday. Over 50 employers are expected to attend the event.
Eighth annual Startup Crawl returns to downtown Fayetteville. The eighth annual Startup Crawl is scheduled to return to downtown Fayetteville on Friday, September 25.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 1, 2026
item.description:
The Centerton Fire Department received two new Pierce Enforcer fire engines.
Centerton Fire Department receives two new fire engines. The Centerton Fire Department announced the arrival of two new Pierce Enforcer fire engines.
Drake Farms opens first apartments for lease. Drake Farms in Fayetteville, a multi-use project on approximately 165 acres, has opened its first apartments for leasing. The first residential units in the development will begin leasing this week.
Benton county judge replacement process faces Thursday deadline. The deadline to begin the process of replacing Austin McCollum as Benton County's unopposed candidate for county judge is Thursday, though the legal deadline for replacement is September 17.
Rogers Library Board of Trustees meeting postponed to September 22. The Rogers Library Board of Trustees meeting, originally scheduled for September 15, has been postponed until September 22.
NWACC academic-credit enrollment increases by 1.8%. NorthWest Arkansas Community College's academic-credit enrollment increased by 1.8% from 2025, with total student enrollment exceeding 12,000 for the first time.
Mercy NWA joins Maternal Life360 initiative. Mercy Hospital Northwest Arkansas, Family Network, and the Arkansas Department of Human Services launched Maternal Life360, a program designed to support healthier pregnancies.

Lawnly to debut Lawn Care Olympics in Fayetteville on September 20. Lawnly, a tech platform for lawn care, will debut the first-ever Lawn Care Olympics in Fayetteville on September 20.

item.description:
The Benton County Quorum Court continued its consideration of an ordinance to establish a fund for the 287(g) program.

American Airlines adds new one-stop flights from XNA to europe in 2027. American Airlines announced it will add new one-stop flights from Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) to several European destinations in 2027.

Bentonville girls golf team wins fort smith tournament. The Bentonville girls golf team won the Fort Smith tournament.

Japanese artist behind Crystal Bridges 'Infinity mirrored Room' dies at 97. Yayoi Kusama, the artist behind the Infinity Room at the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, has died at 97.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 27, 2026
item.description:
Southwest D Street in Bentonville will close until October 2 for infrastructure work.
Southwest D Street in Bentonville to close through October 2. Southwest D Street between Southwest 20th Street and Southwest 24th Street will be closed for infrastructure work until October 2.
Bentonville City Council approves morning star schoolhouse property donation. The Bentonville City Council approved the donation of the Morning Star Schoolhouse property, which the Parks and Recreation Department plans to revitalize.

Triton Ventures opens headquarters in Bentonville. Bentonville AI startup Triton Ventures opened its new headquarters at North ROC, an office and coworking campus.
Scott Family Amazeum to open expansion this fall. The Scott Family Amazeum in Bentonville will open approximately 34,740 square feet of new indoor and outdoor space this fall, adjacent to its existing 50,000-square-foot museum.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.

August sales tax revenue falls in Bentonville, Fayetteville, Rogers, and Springdale. Sales tax revenue reported in August for Bentonville, Fayetteville, Rogers, and Springdale totaled $10.001 million, a 0.12% decrease from the same month last year.
Walton children to be inducted into business hall of fame. Rob Walton, Alice Walton, Jim Walton, and the late John Walton, children of Walmart founders Sam and Helen Walton, will be inducted into the Arkansas Business Hall of Fame.
Rogers City Council meeting cancelled. The Rogers City Council meeting scheduled for September 8, 2026, has been cancelled.
Rogers fire Pension and Relief Board to meet. The Fire Pension and Relief Board will hold a meeting from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM at 301 W. Chestnut Street in Rogers.

item.description:
Bentonville City Council approved amendments to noise regulations, setting new decibel limits and times for music.
Bentonville City Council approves noise regulation amendments. Bentonville City Council approved amendments to noise regulations, which will set specific decibel levels and times for music starting next month.
Northwest Arkansas National Airport board approves construction contract for new concourse. The Northwest Arkansas National Airport board approved a construction contract for a new western concourse and other amenities. The $78.78 million project will add a two-level, approximately 111,000-square-foot expansion on the west side of the terminal.
Rogers City Council approves $3.9 million in federal grant money for street projects. The Rogers City Council approved the acceptance of more than $3 million in federal money for street and road improvements.
Healthcare startups to participate in Northwest Arkansas pilot program. Healthcare startups in Northwest Arkansas have been selected by Arkansas-based healthtech accelerator HTA and startup-connection organization NXTUS Inc. for $20,000 Community Pilot Projects.
Walmart, tyson foods, and autonomous trucking partner announce $200 million in funding. Gatik AI Inc., an autonomous trucking provider with customers including Walmart and Tyson Foods, announced it raised $200 million in a new funding series.
Collier & Associates enters deal to use Compass International technology. Fayetteville-based real estate company Collier & Associates established a private-label partnership with Compass International Holdings, a New York-based real estate services company.
UAMS and NWACC announce partnership to support student athletes. The Northwest Arkansas Community College and University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences signed a memorandum of understanding for UAMS Health to provide annual screening and injury prevention support to NWACC athletes.
University of Arkansas calls off plans for walk-thru 7 brew on campus. The University of Arkansas has called off plans for a new 7 Brew location to open on campus this fall.
Centerton unveils downtown revitalization plan. The City of Centerton unveiled its downtown revitalization plan at a recent City Council meeting.
Thaden School in Bentonville opens new gymnasium. Thaden School in Bentonville cut the ribbon for its new gymnasium.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville, as part of Big Sugar Classic week.

item.description:
The Centerton Planning Commission will consider a final draft of the city's downtown master plan on September 1.
Rogers to have overnight lane closures on West walnut street. Overnight lane closures are scheduled for West Walnut Street in Rogers for a couple of weeks due to a road resurfacing project.

This would allow the city's electric utility to purchase four 161 kV breakers from GE Grid Solutions for $690,400.00 plus tax, without seeking other bids, due to market volatility and long lead times for these products.

Madison county approves three-year data center ban. Madison County approved a three-year moratorium on data center development, joining other counties in the state with similar restrictions.
Two Rogers churches consider land for affordable housing. Two churches in Rogers are considering using their land for affordable housing. Faith organizations in Benton and Washington counties own over 7 square miles of land, with nearly half of it vacant.
Walmart NW Arkansas Championship marks 20th year. The Walmart Northwest Arkansas Championship presented by P&G is celebrating its 20th year. A preview event was held with panels discussing the golf tournament's impact.

Arkansas' longest-running marathon ends. After 50 years, the Hogeye marathon and relays in Northwest Arkansas are being discontinued.
Experience Fayetteville and University of Arkansas to offer new gameday experience. Experience Fayetteville and the University of Arkansas are collaborating to introduce a new gameday experience, including a parade to Razorback Stadium. Fans can also participate in a 'Trailgating' experience connecting downtown and the stadium.

Hogeye Marathon will not continue in 2027. The Hogeye Marathon will not continue in 2027, with organizers planning to focus on shorter races.

Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Gentry mayor plans to retire at year-end. Gentry's mayor plans to retire after this year, leaving the position's future unclear.
Arkansas Music Week returns to Fayetteville August 23-30. Arkansas Music Week will return to Fayetteville from August 23-30 for a week-long celebration of local music, culture, and creativity.
Housing policy runs through Arkansas. Arkansas communities face various housing pressures, with Northwest Arkansas working to keep pace with growth and rural areas struggling to attract builders.
ICE fears impact Northwest Arkansas festivals. Immigrant rights advocates state that fears and backlash related to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement have contributed to lower attendance at Northwest Arkansas festivals.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 23, 2026
item.description:
Bella Vista's renovated City Hall will open on Wednesday, August 26.
Bella Vista City Hall to open after renovation. The renovated Bella Vista City Hall will officially open on Wednesday, August 26.
Benton County experiences widespread power outage. More than 15,000 Carroll Electric customers in Benton County lost power on Saturday afternoon.

This would allow Bentonville Electric Utility Department (BEUD) to purchase four 161 kV breakers from GE Grid Solutions for $690,400.00 plus tax without competitive bidding, due to market volatility and long lead times for these products.

This change in zoning classification for the property at 301 SE B Street could allow for different types of development than currently permitted for suburban single-family homes.

Dodo coffee to open new flagship store in Fayetteville. A Fayetteville coffee shop, Dodo Coffee, is preparing to open its new flagship location.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
100 Black Men of Northwest Arkansas holds informational meeting. The 100 Black Men of Northwest Arkansas held a membership informational meeting at the Fayetteville Public Library for community members interested in the organization.
Northwest Arkansas business briefs include Arvest Bank recognition. Northwest Arkansas business news includes Arvest Bank being recognized on Forbes' list of best employers.
Local cross country season begins this week. The 2026 cross country season is set to begin statewide this week, with Northwest Arkansas' first race, the Shiloh Saints Invitational, scheduled for Saturday.
Fayetteville volleyball team looks to contend for state championship. The Fayetteville Lady Purple Bulldogs, under new leadership, are expected to be contenders for the state volleyball championship after finishing as runner-up last year.
Elkins elks expect to repeat as champions. The Elkins Elks expect to repeat as Class 4A state champions, despite being picked second in 4A-1 behind Gravette.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 22, 2026
item.description:
A portion of Northwest A Street in Bentonville will close Monday for water main repairs.
Bentonville closes Northwest A Street for water main repair. A section of Northwest A Street between Northwest Ninth and Northwest Park streets in Bentonville will be closed from 9 a.m. Monday to 2 a.m. Tuesday for water main repairs.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Council to consider waiving competitive bidding for electrical equipment purchase. This would allow Bentonville Electric Utility Department (BEUD) to purchase four 161 kV breakers from GE Grid Solutions for $690,400.00 plus tax, which are needed for future substation projects.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone property at 301 SE B Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family, to T3.2, Neighborhood Transition. This change in zoning classification could allow for different types of development or density on the property at 301 SE B Street than currently permitted for suburban single-family homes.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to reduce the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This would decrease the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from one percent to one-half of one percent. This change would amend Ordinance No. 2017-15.

This would allow the city to receive a federal grant of up to $3,987,536.00 from the U.S. Department of Transportation for safe streets initiatives. It would also appropriate $4,984,420.00 into the Safe Streets for All (Ss4a) Grant Revenue and Expense accounts.
Northwest Arkansas housing market stabilizes. The Northwest Arkansas housing market is now considered a buyer's market for the first time in five years, with prices beginning to stabilize, according to Arvest's first half of 2026 Skyline report. Home sales continue to increase, though pricing was mixed with average prices declining in Benton and Madison counties but still rising in other areas.
Federal judge rules Arkansas ballot measure laws unconstitutional. A federal judge on Friday ruled several Arkansas laws regarding citizen ballot measures are unconstitutional and issued a permanent injunction against their enforcement.
7hills plans to sell day center for affordable housing. 7hills Homeless Center announced its intention to sell its day center in south Fayetteville to a company that plans to develop affordable housing on the site.
Siloam Springs interim police chief Derek Spicer to retire. Interim Siloam Springs Police Chief Derek Spicer announced his retirement, making him the second Siloam Springs police chief to retire this year. His retirement is planned for next month.
Samaritan community center to host job fair. A Northwest Arkansas nonprofit will host a free job fair next week.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
UA cleans up after water leak at reid hall. A water leak in a University of Arkansas residence hall has displaced students until at least Sunday.
Siloam Springs school district launches podcast. The Siloam Springs School District has launched the Panther Pulse Podcast to keep the community informed about district happenings.
Bentonville panel discusses Marshallese community. A Bentonville panel discussed the Marshallese community in Northwest Arkansas, highlighting efforts to raise awareness about why the region has the largest Marshallese population in the country.

item.description:

Bentonville Planning Commission approves walton STEM university plan. The Bentonville Planning Commission unanimously approved the overarching site plan for a new university campus.

Bentonville School District increases bus driver pay. The Bentonville School Board voted to increase pay for bus drivers after starting the new school year with a shortage.
Rogers school board approves seven Cambridge international courses. The Rogers School Board approved seven new Cambridge courses for middle and high school students, making the district the first in Arkansas to offer the Cambridge Pathway.
Rogers Animal Services offers fee-waived adoptions. The City of Rogers Animal Services is offering fee-waived adoptions for one year after receiving a $6,000 grant from Best Friends Animal Society.
Fayetteville City Council strengthens data center regulations. The Fayetteville City Council unanimously passed an amendment to strengthen the city's data center regulations.
Lake Sequoyah Drive bridge in Fayetteville to close for rehabilitation. The Lake Sequoyah Drive bridge in Fayetteville will temporarily close for several weeks for a rehabilitation project.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
John Brown University receives $34.5 million for health care master's programs. John Brown University announced a $34.5 million gift commitment to launch four new master's degree tracks in health care.
Arvest Bank CFO Karla Payne to retire in early 2027. Arvest Bank Chief Financial Officer Karla Payne will retire in early 2027 after more than 40 years with the company.
Ozark Quilt Fair returns to Springdale museum. The 48th Annual Ozark Quilt Fair will be held on Saturday, September 12, at the Shiloh Museum grounds in downtown Springdale.
Mercy Fort Smith and NWA recognized for heart attack care. Mercy Hospitals Fort Smith and Mercy Hospitals Northwest Arkansas have been recognized by the American College of Cardiology for their heart attack care.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 19, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Planning Commission approved a campus development plan for a business-oriented university focused on STEM.
Heat Advisory issued for Benton County until 9 p.m. Wednesday. The National Weather Service has issued a Heat Advisory for Benton County, effective until 9 p.m. on Wednesday. Heat index values are expected to reach up to 108 degrees.
Bentonville Planning Commission approves Walton STEM university plan. The Bentonville Planning Commission voted 7-0 to approve a campus development plan for a business-oriented university. The university, spearheaded by the Walton family, will focus on science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.
Bentonville School Board plans evening Star elementary expansion. The Bentonville School Board approved preliminary plans to expand Evening Star Elementary School. This expansion aims to accommodate continued growth in student enrollment.
Northwest Arkansas National Airport Connector Road and Springdale Northern Bypass section to open. The Arkansas Department of Transportation has scheduled a ribbon-cutting for Phase Two of the U.S. 412 Springdale Northern Bypass and the new Connector Road to the Northwest Arkansas National Airport. The opening will provide a quicker route to the airport and Oklahoma.

Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of the Big Sugar Classic week.

Community Connections expands services into Northwest Arkansas. Conway-based nonprofit Community Connections is expanding its services to Northwest Arkansas. The organization provides support for children with special needs and their families.
Tyson Foods announces plant closures impacting over 3,000 workers. Tyson Foods will close two plants, affecting more than 3,000 workers. The closures are attributed to a 'historic cattle shortage'.
Northwest Arkansas National Airport sets July enplanement record. Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) recorded its highest monthly number of enplanements in July. More individuals boarded flights during this month than in any previous month on record.

Benton County Quorum Court pauses sales tax reallocation vote. The Benton County Quorum Court will not pursue placing a plan to reallocate county sales tax revenue on the November 3 ballot. This decision follows discussions with mayors in the county.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 15, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory is in effect for Benton County until Saturday evening, with heat index values expected to reach 110 degrees.
NWS tulsa issues heat advisory for Benton county. A heat advisory has been issued for Benton County from August 14 at 10:49 PM CDT until August 16 at 8:00 PM CDT. Heat index values are expected to reach up to 110 degrees on Saturday, with higher values possible on Sunday.

This would allow the Bentonville Utility Board to purchase four 161 kV breakers from GE Grid Solutions for $690,400.00 plus tax, without seeking other bids, for future substation projects. This decision is proposed due to market volatility and long lead times for these products.

This proposed change would allow for a mix of housing types and small-scale commercial uses at 405 NW 5th Street, potentially increasing density and local services in the area.

This proposed ordinance would decrease the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from one percent to one-half of one percent. This means you would pay less tax when purchasing meals and drinks from local establishments.

Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet on August 18. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education is scheduled to meet on August 18, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building. The agenda includes a welcome, call to order, pledge, and approval of the agenda.
Circle of Life to purchase Washington Regional Hospice. Springdale-based Circle of Life will acquire Washington Regional Hospice and its Willard Walker Hospice Home in Fayetteville. Circle of Life is a nonprofit offering hospice and palliative care.
Walmart recalls tomato soup products due to listeria risk. Walmart stores in several states, including Arkansas, are recalling certain tomato soup products due to potential listeria contamination. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration reported the recall.
Fayetteville to close lane on Mission Boulevard for sidewalk construction. One lane of Mission Boulevard in Fayetteville will experience closures for new sidewalk construction beginning August 17. The closures are expected to last for several months.
Tyson Foods beef plant closures to impact communities. Tyson Foods' closure of two beef processing facilities and exploration of selling a third will create significant challenges and uncertainty in the affected communities. This information comes from beef organizations and local elected officials.
NorthWest Arkansas Community college receives $600,000 grant for mentorship. The Northwest Arkansas Community College's LIFE program has received a nearly $600,000 grant from the Walton Family Foundation. This funding will allow the program to expand its mentorship initiatives.
Fayetteville hosts bike helmet giveaway. The City of Fayetteville is hosting a bike helmet giveaway to promote cycling safety. This initiative aims to ensure residents can enjoy cycling safely.
Fayetteville Mayor Rawn appoints new c-suite members. Fayetteville Mayor Molly Rawn has appointed Jennifer Walker as the city’s chief of staff and Keith Macedo as chief information officer. These appointments are effective immediately.
